title: Typography at Scale
description: Learn how to build a cohesive type system using modular scales, responsive sizing with clamp(), font pairing, and CSS custom properties. Transform flat, same-size text into a clear visual hierarchy.

steps.title: Start with one font size
steps.instruction: Imagine a page where every piece of text is 16px. No headings stand out, no captions recede. It is readable but completely flat. This is our starting point—and it shows exactly why a type scale matters. Without size contrast, there is no hierarchy.
steps.code: body { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 16px; line-height: 1.5; color: #121726; } h1, h2, h3, p { font-size: 16px; margin: 0 0 8px; }

steps.title: Create a modular scale
steps.instruction: A modular scale uses a consistent ratio to generate font sizes. We will use a 1.25 ratio (called a "Major Third"). Starting from a 16px base: 16 x 1.25 = 20, 20 x 1.25 = 25, and so on. Each step up feels proportionally larger, creating natural visual rhythm.
steps.code: :root { /* Major Third scale (1.25 ratio) */ --text-xs: 0.8rem; /* 12.8px */ --text-sm: 0.875rem; /* 14px */ --text-base: 1rem; /* 16px */ --text-lg: 1.25rem; /* 20px */ --text-xl: 1.563rem; /* 25px */ --text-2xl: 1.953rem; /* 31.25px */ --text-3xl: 2.441rem; /* 39px */ } h1 { font-size: var(--text-3xl); } h2 { font-size: var(--text-2xl); } h3 { font-size: var(--text-xl); } p { font-size: var(--text-base); }

steps.title: Add responsive sizing with clamp()
steps.instruction: A heading that looks great on desktop can overwhelm a mobile screen. The clamp() function solves this elegantly: you set a minimum, a preferred (fluid) value, and a maximum. The browser picks the right size automatically. No media queries needed for font sizes.
steps.code: :root { /* Fluid type scale with clamp() */ --text-base: clamp( 0.875rem, 0.8rem + 0.25vw, 1rem ); --text-lg: clamp( 1.1rem, 1rem + 0.5vw, 1.25rem ); --text-2xl: clamp( 1.5rem, 1.2rem + 1.5vw, 2rem ); --text-3xl: clamp( 1.8rem, 1.4rem + 2vw, 2.5rem ); }

steps.title: Pair fonts for contrast
steps.instruction: Great typography pairs a distinctive heading font with a highly readable body font. The classic approach: use a serif or geometric sans for headings (personality) and a neutral sans-serif for body text (clarity). Make sure to set appropriate line-heights for each—headings need tighter spacing than body text.
steps.code: :root { --font-heading: 'Georgia', serif; --font-body: 'system-ui', sans-serif; } h1, h2, h3 { font-family: var(--font-heading); line-height: 1.2; letter-spacing: -0.02em; color: #121726; } p, span, li { font-family: var(--font-body); line-height: 1.6; color: #5a6375; }

Body text uses a clean sans-serif for easy reading at smaller sizes. The contrast between heading and body fonts creates visual interest.

steps.title: Complete typography system
steps.instruction: Let's bring everything together into a complete system. Font families, a fluid modular scale, line-heights, and font-weights—all stored as CSS custom properties. This gives you a single source of truth that mirrors text styles in Figma and can be updated from one place.
steps.code: :root { /* Font families */ --font-heading: 'Georgia', serif; --font-body: 'system-ui', sans-serif; --font-mono: 'Menlo', monospace; /* Fluid type scale */ --text-xs: clamp(0.7rem, 0.68rem + 0.15vw, 0.8rem); --text-sm: clamp(0.8rem, 0.77rem + 0.2vw, 0.875rem); --text-base: clamp(0.9rem, 0.85rem + 0.25vw, 1rem); --text-lg: clamp(1.1rem, 1rem + 0.5vw, 1.25rem); --text-xl: clamp(1.3rem, 1.1rem + 1vw, 1.563rem); --text-2xl: clamp(1.5rem, 1.2rem + 1.5vw, 1.953rem); --text-3xl: clamp(1.8rem, 1.4rem + 2vw, 2.441rem); /* Line heights */ --leading-tight: 1.2; --leading-normal: 1.5; --leading-relaxed: 1.65; /* Font weights */ --weight-normal: 400; --weight-medium: 500; --weight-bold: 700; }
